written.q: Define atomic data type and composite data type and give two differences between them.
written.a:
Atomic: a set of non-decomposable data; consists of a set of homogeneous data and a set of operations that can be performed on the data. Composite: a set of decomposable data, composed using atomic and composite data types; could consist of homogeneous or heterogeneous data.

Differences: (1) atomic data cannot be broken down, composite data can; (2) atomic data is homogeneous, composite data may be heterogeneous; (3) composite types are built from atomic and/or other composite types, atomic types are the basic building blocks.

written.q: Define a data structure and explain its data, structure and operations using an array of integers.
written.a: A data structure is a structure that holds a set of atomic or composite data; it consists of a set of homogeneous or heterogeneous data and a set of operations that can be performed on the data. For int num[] = {3, 2, 1}: the data are the integers 3, 2, 1 (atomic, homogeneous); the structure is that they are arranged one after another and reached by index 0, 1, 2 (linear); the operations are get (print num[0]) and set (num[2] = 5).

written.q: Write C++ struct declarations for a Person that has a name (up to 30 characters), a weight and a date of birth made of year, month and date. State which parts are atomic and which are composite.
written.a:
struct Day    { int year; int month; int date; };
struct Person { char name[30]; int weight; Day dob; };

Atomic: year, month, date, weight and the characters of name. Composite: Day (built from atomic ints) and Person (built from atomic types and the composite Day).

written.q: Describe the data structure Person employee[] holding two employees, and give a get and a set operation.
written.a: It is an array of composite elements: heterogeneous (name, weight, date of birth), containing both atomic and composite data, and linear (elements one after another). Get: print employee[0].name;. Set: employee[1].weight = 57;.
